answer: One concrete mechanism: cap per-account emission and put the surplus into a pool earned only by non-duplicate work, because juniper only stays cheap while duplicating content caps out because the pool rewards novelty, not volume. Concretely, sable is enforced in the ledger: Detection is retrospective: payouts for a flagged cluster are clawed back after the fact. Any umber approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
